candidates.theme_relation: Restaurant franchise compounder whose royalty growth depends on franchisee willingness to open new units and maintain strong store-level economics.

candidates.why_include: Franchise growth is capital-constrained, and sale-leaseback providers can become a hidden funding rail for operators. EPRT's 2025 10-K describes a portfolio of single-tenant properties net leased long term to middle-market service-oriented or experience-based businesses, which maps to franchisee/operator capital needs even though restaurants are only one part of its portfolio.

memory_update.text: WING should be retained as a high-signal benchmark for franchisee-unit-economics research because it discloses explicit franchisee return targets, domestic AUV, franchised-unit growth, and development pipeline details.

ARCO adds a customer/operator lens to the franchisee-economics node: it is a large independent McDonald's franchisee and can be used to test whether franchisees can fund openings and remodels under real labor, rent, food, royalty, and FX pressure.

EPRT is a plausible second-order beneficiary and risk monitor for franchisee financing because sale-leaseback capital can fund restaurant growth or balance-sheet repair, but restaurant tenant concentration and rent coverage require verification.

TOST and OLO map to the operational/digital side of franchisee economics rather than restaurant ownership; both need evidence that their products improve AUV, labor productivity, direct-channel mix, or multi-unit management economics.

Need a follow-up pass on other financing and real-estate chokepoints including FCPT, NNN, O, ADC, VICI food-service tenant exposure, private credit providers, and restaurant construction/remodel suppliers; FCPT appeared relevant but was omitted to keep the candidate list at five.

node: Franchisee unit economics and new-unit development
summary: Expanded the universe around the node where restaurant system growth depends on franchisee cash returns, financing capacity, development appetite, and operational/digital tools that improve store-level throughput or margins. The five candidates include one direct franchisor benchmark with unusually explicit franchisee-return disclosure, one large master franchisee/operator, one net-lease capital provider, and two restaurant-technology platforms that may be underappreciated second-order beneficiaries if multi-unit operators prioritize efficiency, digital ordering, and above-store management.
